figures.finding: Puerto Rico's labour relations fall under US federal law: the US National Labor Relations Board's Region 12 covers it, so performers', writers' and directors' unions and agreements there are those of the US system; no Puerto Rican agreement of its own setting an actor's, writer's or director's pay was found.

figures.finding: Puerto Rico gives a transferable production tax credit of up to 40% of payments to Puerto Rico resident companies and individuals and up to 20% of payments to qualified non-resident individuals (who are withheld 20%), for features, shorts, documentaries, TV, music videos and commercials, under the Incentives Code (Act 60-2019); since April 2026 a 15-year Film Productions Master Grant lets experienced producers add successive projects, each drawing on that fiscal year's credit balance, and from 1 July 2026 unapproved applications are dismissed. The credits are capped at USD 100 million per fiscal year (Act 5-2023, up from USD 38 million), with at least 10% reserved for local productions and documentaries.

sources.said: Up to 40% production tax credit on all payments to Puerto Rico Resident Companies & Individuals. Up to 20% production tax credit on all payments to Qualified Nonresident individuals. … If 50% or more of principal photography is shot in the island, development payments to Puerto Rico Resident companies and individuals can qualify. Payments made to Qualified Nonresident individuals are subject to a 20% withholding over the Puerto Rico sourced income.

On April 7, 2026, the Puerto Rico Department of Economic Development and Commerce (“DDEC”) issued Circular Letter No. DDEC 2026-003 … The Circular Letter introduces the Film Productions Master Grant, a new 15-year tax exemption grant … Each successive Film Project added to the Master Grant will be considered subject to the balance of tax credits available for the fiscal year in which it is added. … Producer fee payments must be substantiated through invoices and verifiable proof of payment, such as receipts or canceled checks. These fees are subject to review and must be consistent with prevailing industry standards.
